title: Negation-class parallel Pollard rho on P-256 with a global work meter, an itemised distinguished-report path and prices taken from an executed AArch64 field listing (walk of 5fa78d62)

claims.statement: For the uniform full-production P-256 target Q=[x]P, the classical cold attack in proof.md (negation-class parallel Pollard rho: twisted R=2048 adding walk on classes {P,-P} keyed by x, doubling escapes from detected 2-cycles and checkpoint cycles of length <= 64, distinguished classes routed to 2^16 storage nodes each natively addressable below 2^57 bytes, linear probing capped at 256 probes with the whole report path itemised (probe sequence, full-node test, capacity check, insertion, a 16-edge routed request and a 16-edge response at 16 instructions per word per edge plus 64 control per edge, and the flush) and charged 21.6 units per report, no replacement or eviction, a Chernoff-bounded report count and per-node share, re-walk solving), the walk of submission 5fa78d62-1c6b-46b8-b9cf-02481a49e645 (itself adapted from the class walk of submission 1c600df4), halts on every run after at most 2^127.72 units of C=1000 scalar AArch64 instructions because a global work meter charges every action before it runs; all P-256 arithmetic is charged through the instruction counts of an executed AArch64 listing (field_listing.md, run by experiment.py Part C: Montgomery multiplication M=139, modular addition 20 and subtraction 19 charged A=20, inversion charged I=2^17 against 53,098 executed), giving 1,086 instructions and 1.086 units per step, each other price also its counted instructions divided by 1,000. It succeeds with probability at least 0.39 under the disclosed heuristic H1 (random mapping on N=(r-1)/2 classes with Brent-Pollard correction and a 5% slowdown allowance; index, distinguished and routing bits pseudo-random), supported by toy runs. Peak memory < 2^73 bytes; preprocessing <= 2^60 units, enforced and included; no nonuniform advice. Not a practical break.

experiments.purpose: Part A: production P-256 checks of every identity the walk uses; Part B: the complete per-trail algorithm on prime-order toy curves y^2=x^3-3x+b (T_c census, pipeline success with node routing, long-trail trap test); Part C: executes the AArch64 field listing on production P-256 elements and points (kernel correctness, flag rule, inversion chain, batched additions and doublings) and recomputes the work ledger from the executed counts.
